slice: exploring: the placenta, two selves bi-coupling

items.text: Cells may pass through the placenta between mother and fetus, and male cells go on in some women's brains for several decades: such cells are in more than 60 percent of the brains in one study, in multiple brain regions, and fetal cells are also in blood, lung, thyroid, muscle, liver, heart, kidney and skin; in rats, fetal cells moving to a maternal heart with an injury become heart cells that help repair it. Whether this happens in human brains has no confirmation; whether this is a self touching another directly, or a between going on as two selves' same-existing-society, is the exploring 1.4 meets here.

items.section: 1.3 Every self is a same-existing-society of selves
items.text: The layer of the placenta between mother and fetus is placental cells fusing into one, by syncytin genes, envelope genes of retroviruses entering mammal genomes long ago, separately in the human, mouse and rabbit lineages; in mice, an embryo lacking syncytin-A dies at about day 11.5 to 13.5, and an embryo lacking both syncytins dies at day 9.5 to 10.5: the layer two selves share forms by genes of an old crossing, now in these mammals' own genomes.

items.section: 1.4 A birth release — co-competency distributing the peak
items.text: Fetal trophoblast cells show HLA-C, which maternal KIR receptors bind; the maternal KIR with fetal HLA-C combination goes, with increasing evidence, with how deeply the trophoblast moves into the womb and how far the mother's spiral arteries remodel, setting the placenta's blood flow, and one such combination goes with recurrent miscarriage, fetal growth restriction and pre-eclampsia.

A pregnancy is two selves bi-coupling across a placenta, apart from a self tolerating a non-self: the child's trophoblast cells show HLA-C to the mother's KIR receptors, which goes with how deeply they move into the womb and how far the mother's arteries remodel, the layer between them forms by genes of an old crossing, and cells may pass between mother and child, male cells going on in some women's brains for several decades: a child's cells going on in its mother are, in the five dimensions, the mother's prior other-parity going on now.

items.sentence: Between selves, a same-existing-society co-chains unrelationing two-way, each self pacing its own time and abundancing in no self alone.
items.text: A mother and her fetus are a same-existing-society of two at a placenta: the mother's KIR receptors and the fetus's trophoblast HLA-C go with how far the mother's spiral arteries remodel into the placenta's blood supply, the layer between them forms from cells fusing by genes of an old crossing, and cells may pass between them, male cells going on in some women's brains for several decades.
